venue.name: Fort Rodd Hill and Fisgard Lighthouse National Historic Sites
venue.description: Fort Rodd Hill and Fisgard Lighthouse National Historic Sites, operated by Parks Canada at 603 Fort Rodd Hill Road in Victoria, combine a 19th-century coast artillery fortress that was on active duty from 1895 to 1956 with Fisgard Lighthouse, the oldest lighthouse on Canada's west coast. The grounds include gun batteries, underground magazines and plotting rooms, the Garry Oak Learning Meadow, a historic nature trail and three beaches. Three BC curriculum-based school programs are offered for grades K to 12, each led by a costumed heritage interpreter and including hands-on activities; the school program season runs September to June and programs are available in English, French or a mix. Admission is free for youth 17 and under, and programs run rain or shine.
venue.address: 603 Fort Rodd Hill Road, Victoria, BC V9C 2W8

facility_notes.washrooms: There are washrooms located on site, outside the front kiosk and inside the Fort walls. Children's change tables are available in the gender-inclusive washrooms at the lighthouse and in the women's washrooms at the Second World War Officer's Quarters. The washroom by the main entrance is temporarily closed for renovation.
facility_notes.lunch_space: Picnic areas are available near our parking lot and inside the Fort. There are no indoor eating areas. There is no food or drink available for purchase on site. There is, however, a water fountain.
facility_notes.rain_backup: Our programs run rain or shine. Ensure students are dressed for the weather, including outdoor footwear.
facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: Wheelchair-accessible washrooms are located near the Welcome Centre in the parking lot as well as at the lighthouse; four designated accessible parking stalls are available; a folding, manual wheelchair is available for day use from the Welcome Centre. Because the buildings are protected as culturally significant locations, some areas are not universally accessible: the curved ramp up to the lighthouse has a very steep section with a 27% slope, and many rooms are reached only by a flight of stairs.

restrictions: Emphasize to your group that they cannot climb or stand on old fort walls or buildings.
There is no food or drink available for purchase on site. Please ensure all group members bring a lunch or eat beforehand.
Chaperones and teachers are expected to be available for their students at all times.
Registered service animals are welcome within the site and historic buildings. Please ensure to have your Guide Dog and Service Animal Certification with you when visiting.
venue.hours_notes: October 16 - April 30: 10 am - 4 pm, with Fisgard Lighthouse and historic buildings open Saturday and Sunday only and grounds and washrooms open 7 days a week. May 1 - October 15: 10 am - 5 pm, with the lighthouse, historic buildings, grounds and washrooms open 7 days a week.
venue.seasonal_notes: School program season: September to June. The Canada Strong Pass gave free admission from June 19 to September 7, 2026; regular fees apply as of September 8, 2026.
venue.price_year_or_season: Regular fees as of September 8, 2026 (fees page dated 2025-12-03)

programs.name: Life at the Lighthouse (grades K-6)
programs.description: A curriculum-based school program at Fisgard Lighthouse in which a costumed interpreter teaches students, through games and activities, what life as a lightkeeper was like 150 years ago, how a lighthouse works and why it was built where it was. The teacher information page says school programs run 1.5 hours with no breaks and that groups check in 15 minutes before the scheduled start. The fee is not published: the site says to call or email to book a program and get fee information. Programs are available in English, French or a mix of both.
programs.what_children_do: Children explore Fisgard Lighthouse with a costumed interpreter, play games and do activities about a lightkeeper's daily work, and talk about how weather, the sea and the location shaped the families who lived there.
programs.our_note: The price is the one thing the site will not tell you - you have to phone for it, so ask about the program fee and adult admission in the same call. Everything happens outdoors and in an unheated lighthouse by the ocean, there are no breaks in the ninety minutes, and the site advises a snack outside the kiosk before you start.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms on site and picnic areas outdoors, but no indoor eating area and nothing to buy, so bring lunch and water. Programs run rain or shine in a windy coastal spot, and the program fee, group size limits and chaperone ratio are not published - all worth asking when you phone to book.
programs.payment_timing: Confirm the final number of adults and children in your group and bring your payment to the front kiosk to check in with us.

programs.name: Fit to Serve (grades 7-12)
programs.description: A curriculum-based school program at the fort in which students are assigned to teams and given mental and physical challenges to see if they have what it takes to serve. A costumed interpreter teaches the role of coastal defence and Canada's involvement in the First and Second World Wars, and the hardships faced by the men and women stationed at Fort Rodd Hill. The teacher information page says school programs run 1.5 hours with no breaks and that groups check in 15 minutes early; for the Platoon Challenge tour it asks teachers to arrange students into groups of no more than six before arriving. The fee is not published - call or email to book.
programs.what_children_do: Students work in teams through physical and mental challenges around the fort, practise communicating with military hand signals and Morse code, and try the tests recruits had to pass to enlist.
programs.our_note: This is a moving-around, team-competition program rather than a walk-and-listen tour, so plan for outdoor footwear and weather. The fee is only available by phone, and the site does not publish a maximum group size - ask about both, and about how many chaperones they want.
programs.practical_summary: Outdoor site with washrooms and picnic areas but no indoor eating space and nothing for sale, so bring lunch and water. Programs run rain or shine, and the price, capacity and chaperone expectations are not on the site - confirm by phone.
programs.payment_timing: Confirm the final number of adults and children in your group and bring your payment to the front kiosk to check in with us.

programs.name: WWI Medical (grades 9-12)
programs.description: An immersive school program set in May 1918 at a casualty clearing station in Belgium. Some students take the role of wounded soldiers and others become nurses, guided by two costumed interpreters through the steps of front-line medical treatment and the decisions medical staff had to make. Listed as new on the program descriptions page. School programs run 1.5 hours with no breaks per the teacher information page. The fee is not published - call or email to book.
programs.what_children_do: Students play either a volunteer nurse or a wounded soldier, walk step by step through how casualties were treated at a First World War clearing station, and work in teams to decide the best course of treatment for their patients.
programs.our_note: It is a role-play about battlefield injuries, so it suits a class that is ready for that subject matter. Two interpreters run it, which may affect the fee - and the fee is not published, so phone before you plan a budget.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms and outdoor picnic areas on site, no indoor eating space and no food for sale. The program fee, group size and how far ahead to book are not published, so one phone call settles all three.
programs.payment_timing: Confirm the final number of adults and children in your group and bring your payment to the front kiosk to check in with us.

programs.name: Self-guided visit to the fort and lighthouse
programs.description: A self-guided visit to the two historic sites, entering through the Welcome Centre where groups pay, pick up a site guide and can collect an Xplorers booklet for the children. Visitors tour the gun batteries, underground rooms, the Casemates Barracks exhibits, the Fortress Plotting Room, Fisgard Lighthouse, the Garry Oak Learning Meadow, the Historic Nature Trail and three beaches. Admission is free for youth 17 and under; adults are $10.00 daily, seniors $8.50 and a commercial group is $8.50 per person. Guided tours and special programs are charged separately.
programs.what_children_do: Children walk the paths between the gun batteries, go into the underground magazines and plotting rooms, cross the causeway and climb the stairs inside Fisgard Lighthouse to the upper floor, and follow the packed-gravel trail through the Garry Oak Learning Meadow down to the beaches.
programs.our_note: Free for everyone under 18 makes this one of the cheapest outings in the region - you are only paying for the adults. It is a big outdoor site with stairs, gravel and sea wind, and there is nothing to buy on site, so bring water and lunch and plan on the picnic tables rather than a cafe.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms on site including accessible and gender-inclusive ones with change tables, outdoor picnic areas, and free admission for anyone 17 and under. There are no indoor eating areas, no food for sale, and bus parking is not mentioned anywhere - worth a call before a big group comes.
programs.extra_fees_note: Free admission applies to youth 17 and under. Adults are $10.00 and seniors $8.50 daily; a commercial group is $8.50 per person. Guided tours and programs not usually included with admission are charged separately.
programs.evidence: Free admission for youth 17 and under
